chunk_map.heading: ## Hooks for must-happen, prompts for taste

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 1 (L5): "it runs"/"it exists" resolve same-sentence to "a hook"/"the script". Chunk 2 closest candidate L18 "A menu, not a checklist." -- no proper-noun antecedent, but it is the immediate same-chunk continuation of the demo prompt directly above it (the returned list the prompt asks for), matching the rule's NOT-violation carve-out for immediate continuation of the previous content's subject within one chunk. No never-named or vague-with-full-history referent found in either chunk.

grep -inE 'opening lecture|earlier module|previous lecture|prework' curriculum/lectures/hooks-always-fire.md (lines 1-19 only) -> 0 hits. No sentence in the body points at another file by position; the maintainer/backing provenance notes (L25, L37) are maintainer prose, out of scope for a body-only rule.

Chunk 1 (L5,L7): two self-carrying claims (hooks fire regardless of the agent's say; hooks exist because the LLM forgets). Chunk 2 (L12,L14,L16,L18): the must-happen/taste split, the verifier-to-hook cardinality, the trainer-run demo prompt, and the menu-not-checklist tail. Neither chunk is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet.

Chunk 1 header "Hooks always fire" is borne out by L5 ("the agent has no say in whether it runs ... fires the script whether or not the model remembers it exists"). Chunk 2 header "Hooks for must-happen, prompts for taste" is borne out by L12 ("Must happen goes in a hook; ... taste-shaped stays in a prompt"). Neither header is contradicted by its own chunk's content.

grep -inE '^Not .*\. Not .*\.' body -> 0 hits ("A menu, not a checklist." is a single X-not-Y contrast, not the banned triple). No anaphora/epistrophe triples (no phrase repeated 3x). No self-grading superlatives (no 'most useful/important' language). No number-plus-own-retraction. No abstraction-noun stacks -- L7's "Drift, half-remembered rules" are plain concrete failure-mode nouns, not invented jargon. No verb triplets with an empty leg.

rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -inE 'compendium|forcing function|\bbeat\b|\bmood\b|Connections|writing surface' curriculum/lectures/hooks-always-fire.md (lines 1-19) -> 0 hits. L5/L14 use 'fires'/'primitive' as ordinary Claude Code platform terminology, matching the backing block's own cc-hooks-docs citation for hook events firing -- not maintainer/repo-authorial dialect, appropriate register for AE101's engineer-IC audience.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget -- bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -noE '\*\*[^*]+\*\*' curriculum/lectures/hooks-always-fire.md (body only, lines 1-19) -> two bolds: L5 '**hook**' (1 word, textbook handle) and L12 '**Must happen goes in a hook**' (6 words). Each slide carries exactly one bolded element, within the <=1-per-slide budget. The L12 span is slightly over the ~5-word handle guideline and only its first clause is bolded (the second clause, '; recommended stays in a prompt.', is plain) -- functions as the slide's one named distinction, not the pre-2026-07-09 monoculture of every bullet opening bolded. The harm the rule guards against (decorative bold crowding out true handles) is not present at a single instance on an otherwise unbolded slide.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This is a lecture (mechanism-only, per the maintainer Placement note), so headings should be claims. Chunk 1 header 'Hooks always fire' is a full declarative claim. Chunk 2 header 'Hooks for must-happen, prompts for taste' is an elliptical claim naming the split that governs the whole chunk -- functions as the section's thesis, not a bare label or phase marker.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies -- three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked every prose beat against the three classes (doctrine restatement / self-referential design commentary / aphorism kicker). L5 defines the primitive and names event types (new). L5(cont) explains memory-independence (new mechanism angle). L7 gives the causal WHY (LLM forgetful vs hooks don't forget) -- payoff, not restatement. L12 gives concrete must-happen examples (verifier, pre-commit guard, session-start loader) -- new. L14 introduces the 1:1 verifier-to-hook cardinality -- a new specific claim. L18 'A menu, not a checklist.' is the one piece of information the maintainer block (L27) says neither slide nor prompt otherwise states -- new content, not a koan restating the header.
